title.narrative: Improve access to Integrated Primary Health Care and Nutrition Services for returnees and host communities in areas of returns at Paktia and Helmand provinces.

description.narrative: ltpgtRHDO, with an established operational presence in Helmand and Paktia provinces and technical oversight from its Kabul headquarters, will deliver integrated health, nutrition, MHPSS, and community mobilization services through functional health facilities. The intervention will be implemented in alignment with Health Cluster priorities and in close coordination with MoPH, PPHDs, and cluster partners to avoid duplication and ensure effective service coverage.ltbrgtIn Paktia Province, RHDO operates four service delivery points across three districts: Zahoo BHC in Gardez District serving 6,886 people, Tandan SHC in Gardez District serving 3,591 people, Sheznak SHC in Sayed Karam District serving 5,600 people, and Stoori MHNT in Wazi Zadran District providing outreach services to 8,556 people.ltbrgtIn Helmand Province, RHDO supports three facilities identified in coordination with the PPHD to address major service gaps: Shahzada Health Facility in Sangin District serving 7,700 people, Basir Bazar BHC in Marja District serving 11,130 people, and Zamari Bawrai SHC in Nad Ali District serving 7,028 people.ltbrgtRHDO has already established and activated these health facilities in the newly assigned areas, and health and nutrition services are currently ongoing.ltbrgtImplementation is led by experienced RHDO staff, complemented by targeted recruitment to address technical gaps and ensure gender-balanced teams. RHDO’s established procurement, logistics, and transport systems will ensure the timely supply of medicines and equipment. Community engagement, capacity building, and specialized services will be delivered in line with humanitarian standards.ltbrgtMonitoring and reporting will follow a structured approach with facility-level supervision, provincial monitoring, and HQ oversight. Data will be collected through HMIS and MIS systems, ensuring sex-, age-, and disability-disaggregated data for adaptive management. Community feedback mechanisms under the CRFM will strengthen accountability and service quality.ltbrgtThe project integrates localization, protection, gender equality, and inclusion as cross-cutting priorities. Community and religious leaders will be engaged throughout implementation to promote trust and participation. Feedback mechanisms—including hotlines, suggestion boxes, and community meetings—will ensure Accountability to Affected Populations (AAP) and support continuous improvement of services. ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtRHDO has already established and activated these health facilities in the newly assigned areas, and health and nutrition services are currently ongoing. These health facilities are located farther from previously supported health facilities and are situated in hard-to-reach areas. Additionally, they are positioned within deprived districts of the mentioned provinces. ltbrgtlt/pgt
